lines.trans: Mom, tell me, what is she doing here right now?
Your mom herself invited me to dinner.
It seems to Gulya that you are purposefully setting us up.
Not at all, Lyova decides for himself whom to date.
Exactly, and I have already chosen Gulya.
It is not my fault that I fell in love with this person.
Did you really fall in love with him so quickly?
I understand perfectly well that you want the apartment.
Listen to me carefully, this apartment will be mine.
What are you saying, what are you even talking about?
I have already been looking after his mom for two months.

examples.text: Света, не расстраивайся, Катя поговорит с мамой.
examples.trans: Sveta, do not be upset, Katya will talk to her mom.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Завтра ваша команда снова играет со Спартаком.
examples.trans: Tomorrow your team plays against Spartak again.

examples.text: Поставь завтра на Спартак пятьдесят тысяч.
examples.trans: Put fifty thousand on Spartak tomorrow.

examples.text: Прости, что сегодня утром так вышло.
examples.trans: Sorry that it turned out like this this morning.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Что тебе нужно, говори быстрее.
examples.trans: What do you need, speak faster.

examples.text: Катя, мы так нормально не поговорили.
examples.trans: Katya, we still have not talked properly.

examples.text: Я не хочу говорить на эту тему.
examples.trans: I do not want to talk about this topic.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.text: Почему в зале вообще нет музыки?
examples.trans: Why is there no music in the hall at all?

examples.text: А жизнь вообще очень несправедливая штука!
examples.trans: And life in general is a very unfair thing!

examples.text: Откуда у вас вообще такие странные мысли?
examples.trans: Where do you even get such strange thoughts?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она машину совсем не заметила.
examples.trans: She did not notice the car at all.

examples.text: Денис, дыши спокойно, сейчас вызовем скорую.
examples.trans: Denis, breathe calmly, we will call an ambulance now.

examples.text: Всё нормально, я просто конфетой подавился.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, I just choked on a candy.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже два месяца ухаживаю за его мамой.
examples.trans: I have already been looking after his mom for two months.

examples.text: Через две недели.
examples.trans: In two weeks.

examples.text: Два дома.
examples.trans: Two houses.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'months' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Не пора ли нам пообедать вместе?
examples.trans: Isn't it time for us to have lunch together?

examples.text: Слушай, пойдём сейчас вместе в кафе.
examples.trans: Listen, let us go to a cafe together right now.

examples.text: Это настоящее святое место французской кухни.
examples.trans: This is a true sacred place of French cuisine.

ухаживать.gloss: to court, to woo; to look after

meanings.en: to court, to pay court to
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'хаживать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to court, to woo; to look after'.

examples.text: Я уже два месяца ухаживаю за его мамой.
examples.trans: I have already been looking after his mom for two months.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

examples.text: Она ухаживает за больной мамой.
examples.trans: She looks after her sick mother.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она машину совсем не заметила.
examples.trans: She did not notice the car at all.

examples.text: Завтра ваша команда снова играет со Спартаком.
examples.trans: Tomorrow your team plays against Spartak again.

examples.text: Мы завтра ваших коней легко обыграем.
examples.trans: Tomorrow we will easily beat your horses.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'leave', paired with 'уйти'.

examples.text: Не можешь нормально работать, тогда уходи.
examples.trans: If you cannot work properly, then leave.

examples.text: Так что быстро уходи из моей квартиры!
examples.trans: So get out of my apartment quickly!

examples.text: Мы уходим, раз ты мне не веришь.
examples.trans: We are leaving, since you do not believe me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я прошу, позволь мне сейчас извиниться.
examples.trans: I beg you, allow me to apologize right now.

examples.text: Костя, из-за аварии у нас всё налаживается.
examples.trans: Kostya, because of the accident everything is getting better for us.

examples.text: Извините, я сейчас быстро начну играть.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I will quickly start playing right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты ей ещё сто тысяч должен.
examples.trans: You still owe her a hundred thousand.

examples.text: А ещё он моя главная опора.
examples.trans: And he is also my main support.

examples.text: Давайте добавим сюда ещё одно красивое слово.
examples.trans: Let us add one more beautiful word here.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we shall see', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.text: Можно я посмотрю?
examples.trans: May I have a look?

examples.text: Я только посмотрел.
examples.trans: I only had a look.

examples.text: А можно я пойду посмотрю?
examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'whose', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Чей это холодильник?
examples.trans: Whose fridge is this?

examples.text: Чья это машина?
examples.trans: Whose car is that?

examples.text: Курица? Нет. А чей это холодильник?
examples.trans: Chicken? No. And whose fridge is this?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Виктор, ты этот тонкий намёк понял?
examples.trans: Viktor, did you understand that subtle hint?

examples.text: Ой, это просто настоящий детский сад.
examples.trans: Oh, this is just a real kindergarten.

examples.text: Атмосфера этого ресторана подкупает каждого гостя.
examples.trans: The atmosphere of this restaurant wins over every guest.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'зволить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will allow', paired with 'позволять'.

examples.text: Позвольте, я сделаю удобнее.
examples.trans: Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

examples.text: Позвольте вам помочь.
examples.trans: Allow me to help you.

examples.text: Прошу, присаживайтесь. Позвольте, я сделаю удобнее.
examples.trans: Please, have a seat. Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.
